clue.text: Create "Ye Glum Old Sailor"? Somehow he did!

definitions.text: Create "Ye Glum Old Sailor"? Somehow he did!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are got into shape by some unstated means, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A challenge to write about a gloomy old seaman, answered by the man who actually managed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges all of CREATE YE GLUM OLD SAILOR (21 letters). The whole clue is also the definition: the poet created the Ancient Mariner, the gloomiest old sailor in English verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, whose haunted old seaman fits the quoted description.

clue.text: Jesuits get frenzied without a bishop and hide cat!

parts.note: SJ, Society of Jesus, the letters after a Jesuit's name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: running amok is acting in a frenzy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Jesuits going wild minus a bishop, ending with an exclamation about leather and a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the frenzy word goes round the bishop's letter. 'cat' suggests an animal but means a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A sjambok is a heavy South African whip of rhinoceros or hippo hide, a cat in the sense of a cat-o'-nine-tails.

clue.text: Film director's note: "Hold everything!"

indicators.note: one piece holds, that is contains, the other

parts.note: ME (or mi) is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale
all means everything

explanation.surface: A film director's memo shouting for everything to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like the director calling a halt on set, but it is the container signal. ME as a spelling of the note mi is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Malle was the French director of films such as Au Revoir les Enfants.

clue.text: Capricious apostate! Idle bounder!

definitions.meaning: one who strays or wanders from the faith, an old sense of the word as a noun
a geological boulder carried far by ice, now lying idle where it was dumped

explanation.surface: A string of insults hurled at a fickle renegade who lazes about.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the adjective, the old noun for a wanderer from the true path, and the geologist's term for a stray boulder (with 'bounder' standing in for it).
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unpredictable; as a noun it names a wanderer and a glacier-borne boulder resting far from home.

clue.text: Spike one's dram?

definitions.meaning: to spike a plan is to put a stop to it
a dram is a measure of whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: Asking whether to lace one's glass of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to thwart or stop, like spiking a story; Scotch is whisky, drunk by the dram.

clue.text: Crop of redundancies at Henley?

definitions.meaning: a crop is a short haircut
Henley is the famous English rowing regatta, so job cuts there would be cuts to a rowing team

explanation.surface: A round of layoffs at the Henley regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut; read as two words it is a reduction in a rowing team.

clue.text: Idly examine one bottle left within

indicators.note: within says the following pieces go inside the first

parts.note: to try a case is to examine it in court
I is the Roman numeral one
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: Lazily inspecting a single bottle that was left inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' marks the container: the three short pieces sit together inside the word for examine.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something trivially means doing it in a frivolous, unimportant way, which is acting idly.

clue.text: Well-nourished senior G-man

parts.note: high means senior in rank, as in a high official
a G-man is an FBI agent, a Fed in US slang

explanation.surface: A top FBI agent who eats well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone high-fed has been given rich food in plenty, so they are well nourished.

clue.text: Would speak of return to work with the backing of the Mills Brothers

definitions.text: the backing of the Mills Brothers

indicators.note: return means the heard word is then read backwards
speak of says we want the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: the word would is said aloud and heard as a word for timber
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Describing a comeback to work accompanied by a famous vocal group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speak of' marks the homophone and 'return' then reads the heard word backwards. The Mills Brothers were an American close-harmony vocal group.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is the close-harmony vocal backing style associated with groups like the Mills Brothers.

clue.text: See 1
But it is!

parts.note: a 'but' is a protest raised against something, and in grammar 'it' is the receiving word of a verb, so the term covers both

explanation.surface: An indignant retort in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is to say 'but'; the noun sense describes 'it' as a thing or grammatical complement.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to say 'but'; and 'it' is a thing, or the grammatical receiver of a verb.

clue.text: Bible reformer with the old stony face imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the
a cliff is a face of rock

explanation.surface: A Bible reformer jailed alongside an old man with a hard expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' marks the container: the rock face is shut inside the archaic article. 'stony face' suggests a stern expression but means a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wycliffe led the first translation of the whole Bible into English and was an early church reformer.

clue.text: Did the late Yorick top himself with it?

definitions.text: Did the late Yorick top himself with it?

parts.words: Did the late Yorick top himself with it?
parts.note: Yorick is the dead jester whose bare skull Hamlet holds; 'top himself' suggests suicide but here means cover his head

explanation.surface: A grim question about whether Hamlet's dead jester killed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top himself' looks like suicide; it means put a covering on his top, and Yorick is now only a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cap covering the crown of the head, which on poor Yorick would sit on bare bone.

clue.text: Man of fashion fled in panic after royal rebuff

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
read as re-buff, polishing back, so the word turns round

parts.note: regal means royal

indicators.note: in panic means the letters run about wildly

explanation.surface: A fashionable man running off in alarm after being snubbed by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuff' reverses REGAL to LAGER; 'in panic' scrambles FLED to FELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Lagerfeld was the German designer who led Chanel for decades.

clue.text: Forgers at work here in El Greco's view

definitions.meaning: the Spanish city was famous for forging fine sword blades
El Greco painted the famous View of the city in a storm

explanation.surface: Art forgers busily faking a scene painted by El Greco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgers' suggests art fakers; it means smiths forging steel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish city was renowned for its steel swords and is the subject of El Greco's landscape.

clue.text: Hothead's class of yacht

definitions.meaning: a fire-breathing beast, or a fierce, quick-tempered person
a well-known one-design racing keelboat class

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered man's sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing monster or fierce person, and also the name of an Olympic keelboat class.

clue.text: Children's author at the end of the road without a new series

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece wraps the rest

parts.words: at the end of the road
parts.note: all roads lead to Rome, so the city is where every road ends
S is an abbreviation for series

explanation.surface: A children's writer living at the far end of the street, missing a new book series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: ROME goes round A + N + S. 'All roads lead to Rome' gives the city as the road's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome wrote the Swallows and Amazons books for children.

clue.text: Nymphs' names around before Psyche

definitions.note: the plural possessive stands for the plural name of the sea nymphs, with 's' as a link

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so NS for names
ere is a poetic word for before
the id is part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: Nymphs' names placed around something before the goddess Psyche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' marks the container. 'Psyche' looks like the mythical heroine but means the mind, part of which Freud called the id.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nereids were the sea nymphs of Greek myth, daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: Home ground for strictly personal development?

definitions.text: Home ground for strictly personal development?

parts.words: Home ground for strictly personal development?
parts.note: the plot behind one's own house, where any building is only one's own business, the not-in-my-yard sense

explanation.surface: A question about where private building should go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' suggests self-improvement; it means building on land, kept to one's own patch.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden or yard behind a house is one's own home ground.

clue.text: Grew old and died raising wine for sale here

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: aged means grew old
OB is short for obiit, Latin for died

explanation.surface: Someone aged and died while raising wine to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses AGED + OB (from 'and died') as a whole, upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar where wine is sold.

clue.text: En which to cook oeufs tart?

definitions.meaning: eggs are cooked en ..., in a small ovenproof dish
tart as a slang word for a loose woman, a French courtesan

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank on French egg cookery, ending in a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' suggests pastry but is the old sense of a kept woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocotte is an individual ovenproof dish, and also a French term for a prostitute or courtesan.

clue.text: What cereal smugglers do on the Manchester Ship Canal?

definitions.meaning: smugglers run goods, so grain smugglers would run grain
a town in Cheshire, north-west England, on the canal

explanation.surface: Asking what grain smugglers do along a canal near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Running corn is smuggling grain, and Runcorn is a Cheshire town on the Manchester Ship Canal.

clue.text: Rare find uncovered beyond the rainbow's end

indicators.note: uncovered suggests the letters are dug up and shaken out of their order

explanation.surface: A rare find dug up past the end of the rainbow, like a pot of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' rearranges RARE FIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared radiation lies just past the red end of the visible spectrum.

clue.text: Memorials here to the Queensland Terriers?

definitions.meaning: piles of stones raised as markers
a city in northern Queensland, Australia

explanation.surface: A memorial in Australia to some terriers.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: stone memorials, the Queensland city, and the breed of terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone mounds raised as memorials share the name of the Queensland city and the Scottish terrier breed.

clue.text: Tennyson wrote the same lines about "Journey's End"

parts.note: ID is short for idem, Latin for the same

indicators.note: End picks the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL for lines

explanation.surface: Tennyson wrote the same lines on a famous war play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' takes the last letter of 'Journey's' and 'about' puts the pair of lines round it. Journey's End is R. C. Sherriff's First World War play.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson wrote the Idylls of the King, so one of them is a thing he wrote.

clue.text: Composer recalled one to gory accident

indicators.note: accident suggests the letters are thrown together in a smash

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer recalled to a gory accident scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' rearranges RECALLED + I + TO + GORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was an English composer, best known for Hiawatha's Wedding Feast.

clue.text: The Spanish O'Connor taking time with first-born

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

explanation.surface: A Spanish O'Connor taking time with a firstborn child.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a long-running British TV host and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-born child is the oldest of the family.

clue.text: Post-1989 activities here extramural?

parts.note: after the Wall fell in 1989 activity in this city no longer had a wall dividing it, so it was literally outside the walls

explanation.surface: Asking where adult-education classes happened after 1989.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extramural' suggests evening classes; read literally it means beyond a wall, the one that fell in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: The German capital was divided by its Wall until November 1989.
